title.narrative: WI 2021-2024 Source to Sea: Eastern Africa Wetland Initiative
WI 2021-2024 Source to Sea: Eastern Africa Wetland Initiative

description.narrative:
Den föreslagna insatsen syftar till att avancera Wetlands International (WI) tidigare uppnådda resultat för att skydda och restaurera våtmarker för att därigenom uppnå våtmarkernas fulla potential och värde genom att använda ett ekosystem baserat inkluderande angreppssätt innefattande hela landskap. Insatsen fokuserar främst på bevarande av våtmarker i två identifierade ekoregioner. Kunskapsuppbyggnad utgör ett fundament vilken ska inspirera och mobilisera lokala samhällen och andra lokala sakägare att att utveckla en gemensam vision vilken i sin tur leder till demonstrationsprojekt och integrerade förvaltningsplaner vilka skyddar den biologiska mångfalden och optimerar en hållbar användning av naturresurser. Generellt så ska den föreslagna insatsen adressera drivkrafterna för förlusten av våtmarker och deras betydelse för den biologiska mångfalden i östra Afrika genom att skapa förutsättningar för lösningar för en integrerad förvaltning av våtmarker och landskap av en ekoregional storlek.
Insatsen är specifikt uppdelad på fem sinsemellan relaterade arbetspaket där varje paket har korresponderande utfall vilka i kombination ska leverera till effektmålet. Det finns också en överbryggande lednings- och koordinations komponent vilken utgör det femte arbetspaketet. Arbetspaketten är följande: 1) Kunskapssamlande och kunskapsspridning med det särskilda målet att utveckla och sprida information om ekologisk status, förekomst samt värdet av våtmarkerna i Östafrika med särskilt fokus på Rift valley och ekoregioner för mangrove inom fyra specifika områden inom detta. 2) Stärkande av institutionell uppbyggnad och kapacitetsutveckling med ett särskilt mål för att utveckla kapaciteten hos statliga myndigheter, utbildningsinstitut och det civila samhället inom våtmarker och förvaltning av den biologiska mångfalden baserat på identifierade behov. 3) praktisk lokal insats med det specifika målet att utveckla och arbeta mot en gemensam vision för en integrerad förvaltning för vart och ett av de fyra utvalda landskapen (Ziway-Shalla, Orno-Turkana, Lamu och Rufiju). Detta bygger på existerande lokala sakägarnätverk vilka inkluderar lokala samhällen, statligt anställda och representanter från den privata sektorn. WI ska samarbeta för att hitta en utvecklingsväg för att visionen bestående av komplementära åtgärder för bevarande, restaurering, bättre försörjningsmöjligheter och hållbar utveckling. 4) Sätta Våtmarker och bevarande av den biologiska mångfalden som huvudfåra i regionala, nationella och sub-nationella policy ramverk med målet att stärka existerande regionala nätverk vilka är inbegripna i en hållbar förvaltning av våtmarker. WI ska arbeta med dessa för att tillsammans utarbeta en långsiktig vision för bevarande och restaurering av Rift valley respektive kust ekoregioner av mangove. 5) Programstyrning och koordinering vilket har som mål att säkra en effektiv koordination och styrning av programmet. Detta inkluderar mobilisering av programteamet, samordning mellan arbetspaketen och kontoren samt att säkra tidsutsatt programövervakning och utvärdering och utgöra en givarlänk. En anpassad styrning kommer att tillämpas där programaktiviteterna är i överenssstämmelse med de ändringar som görs baserat på yttre påverkansfaktorer och framväxande insikter och möjligheter. Beskrivningen i denna bedömning speglar en insats som ska genomföras av Wetlands International (WI) under en tre-års period (2021-2024) av ett totalt belopp på 64 201 200 SEK vilket ska finansieras av Sida.

The intervention seeks to advance previous achievements of Wetlands International (WI) to safeguard and restore wetlands for their full range of values using ecosystem-based, inclusive approaches across whole landscapes. It primarily focuses on conservation of wetland in the identified two ecoregions using knowledge as a foundation through inspiring and mobilizing communities and other local stakeholders to develop a common vision, leading to demonstration projects and integrated management plans which safeguard biodiversity and optimise sustainable use of natural resources. In general, the proposed intervention will address the drivers to loss of wetlands and their biodiversity in Eastern Africa by putting in place enabling conditions for integrated wetland management solutions at landscape and ecoregional scales.
Specifically, the proposed intervention is divided in to five inter-connected work packages that each have corresponding outcomes, which combine together to deliver impact. There is also an overarching management and coordination component considered to be the fifth work package. The work packages are: 1) Knowledge generation and dissemination: with a specific objective of developing and disseminating information on trends in status, distribution and values of wetlands in Eastern Africa, with a specific focus on the Rift valley and East African mangroves ecoregions and the 4 target sites therein. 2) Institutional strengthening and capacity development: with a specific objective of strengthening the capacities of government agencies, knowledge institutes and civil society in wetland and biodiversity management based on identified needs. 3) On the ground intervention: with a specific objective of developing and working towards a joint vision for the integrated management in each of the four selected wetland landscapes (Ziway-Shalla, Omo-Turkana, Lamu, Rufiji). Building on existing local stakeholder networks, involving local communities, government officials and private sector representatives, we will collaboratively develop a pathway towards achieving this vision, consisting of a set of complementary conservation, restoration, livelihoods, and sustainable development interventions. 4) Mainstream wetland and biodiversity conservation into regional, national and sub-national policy frameworks: with the objective of strengthening existing regional networks involved in the management of wetlands and will work with them to collectively develop a long-term vision for the conservation and restoration of the Rift valley and Mangrove Coast Ecoregions respectively. 5) Programme management and coordination: with the objective of ensuring the efficient coordination and management of the Programme. This includes mobilizing the programme team, coordinating between work packages and offices, ensuring timely M&E and donor liaison. An adaptive management approach will be adopted, where programme activities are aligned based on changes in the external environment and emerging insights and opportunities.
The details in this appraisal reflects a contribution to be implemented by Wetlands International (WI) in a period of three years (2021 - 2024) with a total sum of 64 201 200 SEK, all of which will be contributed by Sida.

The overall objective of the proposed initiative is to ensure that by 2024, government agencies, civil society and community groups jointly safeguard and restore wetlands of the Rift Valley Lakes and East African Mangrove ecoregions. These ecoregions are amongst the highest priority in Eastern Africa, considering their high biodiversity, ecosystem services and cultural values. The major activities of the proposed intervention will focus on five, inter-connected work packages that correspond to the four outcomes of the programme, each representing a set of milestones and underlying activities. The five focus areas are: (1) Knowledge generation and dissemination, (2) Institutional strengthening and capacity development, (3) on the ground intervention (Integrated landscape regeneration and livelihood enhancement), (4) mainstreaming wetland and biodiversity conservation into regional, national and sub-national policy frameworks, (5) Programme management and coordination: with the objective of ensuring the efficient coordination and management of the proposed intervention.

title.narrative: Grant Agreement between Sida and Wetlands International

description.narrative:
The Source to Sea project marked substantial milestones in wetlands management in the two identified eco-regions namely - the Rift Valley Lakes eco-region (with field interventions in Ziway-Shalla and Omo-Turkana Basins) and the East African Mangrove eco-region (with field interventions in Lamu and Rufiji Delta).
Building on the strong foundation established in the previous years, the Source to Sea Initiative realized significant achievements in the Rift Valley and mangrove ecoregions, within the four key landscapes: Ziway Shalla sub-basin, Omo-Turkana basin, Lamu land and seascape and Rufiji Delta.
Through strategic collaborations with experts and stakeholders in the project areas, the contribution laid a strong foundation for the application of advanced technologies in wetland inventories and established a biodiversity monitoring framework. The different tools deployed to engage stakeholders such as targeted events, dialogues, and knowledge-sharing initiatives has positively influenced stakeholders perceptions and approaches to wetland management.
Capacity-building efforts encompassing hands-on training in restoration techniques, the formation of community support groups, and peer-to-peer learning exchanges were central to the project success. In general, the Source to Sea (S2S) initiative, has contributed to the rehabilitation of over 3,650 hectares of degraded land and the implementation of diverse livelihood interventions addressing more than 22,000 people.
The policy advocacy and analysis work continue to create an enabling environment for the scaling up of wetland restoration efforts. Over the life of the project, it was possible to effectively mobilize and engage stakeholders across both ecoregions, building strong partnerships and earning a reputation as a trusted leader in wetland landscape restoration and sustainable livelihoods.
Work Package I: Knowledge Development and Dissemination
Work Package I focuses on building and sharing of knowledge and experiences. The write-shops, knowledge fairs, and other tools have significantly enhanced the visibility of the contribution on the regional and global stage, allowing stakeholders to build valuable relationships with potential decision-makers and influential individuals within the sector. These events have provided a platform for crucial dialogues centered around case studies and knowledge exchange, serving as a springboard to influence policies, practices, and attitudes at various levels.
The tangible results of these efforts as our knowledge development and dissemination activities are now translating into meaningful change in policy and practice. Notable examples include:
Lamu Climate Action Plan: the climate change vulnerability assessment directly contributed to the development of Lamu's climate action plan, demonstrating a clear and measurable impact on local policy. GMW Data in Action: The establishment of a command center in Lamu signifies the active use of GMW data to inform management practices, ensuring decisions are based on real-time information Up-scaling Best Practices: The S2S initiative played a pivotal role in facilitating the development of best practices, which were consolidated through targeted write-shops. These practices are now ready for wider implementation across different landscapes, ensuring broader environmental benefits. Technical resources: Tools such as NMERG, nursery guidelines and the Lamu Harvest Plan are strengthening evidence-based conservation and management.
Work Package II: Capacity Building
Work Package II focuses on strengthening the capacity of stakeholders at different levels. Targeted support and peer-to-peer learning activities has contributed significantly to create a highly engaged network of partners and stakeholders who are actively advancing a shared mission and vision. Partners demonstrated increased capacity to identify opportunities, mobilize resources for wetland conservation, and raise awareness on the importance of wetlands and landscape-scale restoration. Across four landscapes, the capacity of more than 950 people was built on a wide range of wetland conservation and restoration issues, contributing to stronger collaboration and more effective, collective action.
The work package focuses on training stakeholders and partners, Enhancing skills and knowledge within Wetlands International, Institutional Capacity Building and Community learning exchanges. While building capacity for sustainability, investing in our stakeholders' capacity yielded significant results:
Deeper understanding: Training and awareness-raising sessions strengthened stakeholders understanding of the landscape approach, particularly among government officials and community-based organizations, enabling more effective participation in on-the-ground actions for wetland protection and rehabilitation. Sustainable impact: Strengthened stakeholder capacity has enhanced the long-term sustainability of interventions by equipping local actors with the knowledge and skills required to sustain and advance restoration initiatives beyond direct project involvement. Improved governance: Capacity-building efforts have strengthened governance of supportive activities, enabling more efficient and effective use of resources. Stronger collaboration: Equipping partners with a clear understanding of the vision has fostered a more collaborative environment, attracting broader support for wetland conservation and restoration efforts.
Work package III: Ecological Restoration and Livelihood Enhancement
Landscape rehabilitation efforts have yielded significant results in combating watershed degradation while Community-Based Ecological Mangrove Restoration approach has successfully restored degraded mangrove areas, promoting healthy ecosystems and biodiversity. In total, more than 3,500 hectares are under rehabilitation.
Recognizing the link between livelihoods and environmental pressure, alternative income generating schemes introduced to reduce dependency and pressure on wetlands. This includes promoting beekeeping, sustainable fishing practices, poultry farming, and the use of energy-efficient cook-stoves. These diversified livelihoods provide economic opportunities for communities while safeguarding vital wetland ecosystems.
Rangeland reseeding activities have been introduced understanding the needs of different communities in the different landscapes, including pastoralists. This creates sustainable grazing resources for cattle, reducing pressure on wetlands and fostering a more balanced human-environment relationship. In total, through the project the livelihoods of more than 22,000 people have been improved.
The landscape vision development process has seen positive advancements in all four landscapes. In the process it was learned that there are many ways to develop landscape visions and plans. This has given the opportunity to experiment the different methods in different landscapes.
Overall, by reducing reliance on activities that harm natural habitats, this holistic approach demonstrably led to landscape rehabilitation, improved lives by enhancing micro-climates, reducing soil erosion and flooding, improving access to food and water security, boosting agricultural productivity, and fostering sustainable livelihoods. These combined impacts showcased the transformative power of restoration and livelihood enhancement initiatives, creating a more prosperous future for communities and a healthier environment for all.
Work Package IV: Wetland and Biodiversity Conservation Policy Frameworks
Through building capacity within local communities and ensuring continued monitoring and adaptive management practices, the project fostered a culture of environmental stewardship that transcends generations. This comprehensive approach, combining partnerships, policy, and community engagement, was essential for achieving tangible outcomes.
In all 3 countries, Ethiopia, Kenya and Tanzania, the contribution actively engaged in policy dialogue, sharing S2S lessons and best practices to ensure adoption in policy. A wide variety of Policy briefs has been developed to influence policy and public thinking. Actively participated in national and sub-national dialogues. These are long term processes. We saw a recognition of our expertise on wetlands, biodiversity, and are seeing the first concrete impacts of our engagement in policy processes. For example, we developed national targets for Kenya's National Biodiversity Strategic Action Plan. Under target 2 on ecosystem restoration, we ensured the inclusion of tools for mangrove restoration and conservation to guide wetland restoration efforts. The contribution played a significant role in the development of the Wetlands Restoration Strategy 2023-2032 Kenya. Wetlands stakeholder platform has been established in Tanzania together with NEMC, which will serve as a platform for national-level dialogue on the development of institutional framework for wetland management. Similarly, a multi-stakeholder platform has been re-initiated in the Rift Valley. The proposed draft Rift Valley Vision has been developed by the Platform members. This was a first step to a more coherent ecoregional management of the Rift Valley. In Lamu, project contributed to the County Climate Change Action Plan, which adheres to Financing Locally Led Climate Action principles. As a result, Lamu County was well-equipped to access climate change financing opportunities, both nationally and locally Active engagement in the National Mangrove Management Committee of Kenya, allowing the project to advocate for adoption of best practices throughout the mangrove coast of Kenya. At mangrove Eco-regional level, the project contributed to the Regional Mangrove Action Plan, and actively shared lessons and best practices from S2S in the ecoregion.
Work Package V: Programme Coordination
Institutional capacity of WI and its implementing partners located in the four landscapes has been strengthen. The MERL trainings provided at different intervals has equipped the WI staffs to effectively monitor and evaluate our projects. The resulting MERL system provided us with crucial data to track progress, measure the impact of our interventions and inform adaptive management for ongoing improvement. Open and transparent communication has been established. The S2S communication strategy developed at the start of the project assisted to establish a solid foundation for disseminating information, results on our interventions and visibility materials through established channels.
